title: Hinton explains 'feed the kitty'
summary: Hinton explains for the record the tip box tradition and asks Leeman to talk about Harold West and Clyde Hart.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Hey, Cliff, that part made me feel hungry, too; man, I could just taste that food right now, it must have been delightful. I just want to make this one little statement here. You know, when you're in the kitchen now and you're talking about -- this is just for the future people who are listening to this, you mentioned that you left the pot on the stove and you left a note saying 'feed the kitty'. We would like the people to know that in our day, we used to put a little box up on the bandstand when the musicians were playing -- or a little hat or box or

something, and this was for people who wanted to tip us, help us with some financial aid, and we would say, 'feed the kitty'. So we'd put this box up in front of the bandstand and people would put a buck or two, a five or a ten or whatever was their choice, in there.

So just for the record, when you left that little thing in the kitchen that said feed the kitty, you didn't mean for them to take the food and give it to the cat -- you meant for them to lay some change when they got through eating and cleaned up their dishes, to leave a little money so you could be reimbursed for the food.
So now on to your great friend and mine, Ben Webster, the great saxophone player -- tenor sax.

Excuse me, Cliff -- before you get to Ben, you told me to remind you that you wanted to talk about your partner, chef, the great drummer, Harold West. He was a great drummer at that time, and you wanted to -- he was the one who cooked all those ham hocks and beans, and you said you wanted to talk about some of his drumming and the reasons why he didn't stay around. And you also wanted to mention something about Clyde Hart, the great pianist that was working with you. He was such a great arranger and a great pianist.
So would you go and elaborate on that, please?
